samples.summary: Near-vacuous fourth `normalizeStyleClears` test duplicates the first one and asserts almost nothing new
samples.evidence: `it('leaves an absent color key absent …')` calls `normalizeStyleClears({ backgroundColor: '' })` — the exact input of the first test at line 117 — and only asserts `'color' in result` is false. Since the implementation spreads the caller's object (`normalized ??= { ...style }`), a key that was never in the input can only be absent; the assertion holds for any spread-based implementation and would only fail for a hypothetical implementation that fabricates a fixed keyset. It reads as coverage of the "absent means do not touch" contract but does not exercise the contract that matters: that a *style patch containing a real color plus an empty one* keeps the real one and that the returned object is not the caller's object being mutated.

samples.summary: No test that `normalizeStyleClears` does not mutate the caller's style object
samples.evidence: The helper deliberately copies (`normalized ??= { ...style }`) and returns the original identity when nothing changes. The identity path is asserted (types.test.ts:130 `toBe(style)`), but the copy path has no assertion that the input object was left untouched — e.g. passing `const s = { backgroundColor: '' }` and asserting `s.backgroundColor === ''` afterwards. Callers such as `applyInlineStyle` and `applyStyleInTree` receive style objects owned by toolbar/pending-style state, so silent mutation would be a real regression with no failing test.

samples.summary: The "heals runs that already store `''`" behavior claimed by the task doc has no test
samples.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260817-docs-highlight-none-clear-todo.md:27 states normalizing at the write boundary "also heals runs that already store `''` the next time the user clears them". Both new block-helpers tests build the `''` state by first applying a real color and then clearing, so they never start from a block whose inline already carries `backgroundColor: ''` (the pre-existing corrupted documents the fix is meant to heal). No test seeds `makeBlock` inlines with `style: { backgroundColor: '' }` and asserts the run re-merges after a clear.

samples.summary: Yorkie path tested only for `backgroundColor: ''`; `color: ''` and run re-merge in the Tree are untested
samples.evidence: The two new tests in yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:672-693 both style the whole block, so they only prove the attribute is removed from a single inline. Nothing asserts the other clearable key (`color: ''`) is removed via `removedInlineStyleAttrs` on the Tree path, and nothing asserts the sub-range case where clearing `''` on a partially-styled block lets the runs re-merge back into one inline on reread — the actual user-visible symptom of #793 in the CRDT store. `CLEARABLE_COLOR_KEYS` has two entries; only one is covered here.

samples.summary: Collapsed-cursor (pending style) route for a picker's `''` is untested
samples.evidence: `createPendingStyle.set` stores the raw patch (`{ ...style }`), so clicking the highlight "None" with a collapsed cursor parks `{ backgroundColor: '' }` in pending state; it is only normalized later when `consumeForInsert` reaches `doc.applyInlineStyle`. No test in packages/docs/test/view/pending-style*.test.ts exercises an empty-string color through pending style (e.g. asserting the newly typed text carries no `backgroundColor` key and that toolbar summaries derived from pending state do not report a highlight). The diff's coverage is limited to the two immediate write boundaries.
